docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Tokens and specs provide 10 non-deprecated token sets: 5 standard sizes and 5 connected sizes.
  • Standard sets define per-size container height, between-space, and pressed-width motion tokens.
  • Connected sets define per-size container height, 2dp between-space, fully rounded container shape, and inner-corner tokens.
  • Measurements specify standard inner padding by size and fixed connected padding of 2dp at all sizes.
  • XS and S connected groups must keep a 48dp minimum width and 48x48dp target area.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Use separate token models for standard and connected variants; they do not share spacing or corner behavior.
  • For standard groups, apply size-specific between-space (18/12/8/8/8dp) plus pressed-width animation tokens (dampening, stiffness, width.multiplier).
  • For connected groups, enforce 2dp between-space at all sizes, fully rounded outer container shape, and size-driven inner-corner values.
  • Preserve selected inner corner value at 50% across all connected sizes.
  • Enforce 48dp minimum width and target area rules for connected XS/S variants.

docs.text:
• Material Design 3 button component specifications covering five color variants (Elevated, Filled, Tonal, Outlined, Text) and five size variants (XSmall, Small, Medium, Large, XLarge).

  • Elevation, typography, shape, and layout tokens extracted from Light theme + Default contrast context.
  • Shape morphing uses spring animations with 0.9 damping and 1400 stiffness across all sizes.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Buttons support five style variants: Elevated (shadow), Filled, Tonal, Outlined, and Text-only.
  • All button sizes support optional icon placement before or after the label, using computed icon spacing based on height.
  • Shape morphing on press uses spring animation to smoothly transition from resting shape to a temporary morph value, returning on release.
  • Toggle button functionality is available for all color variants, with distinct unselected and selected container/label/icon colors.
  • Elevation values only apply to Elevated and (deprecated) Filled Hovered state; other variants use shadow colors for visual separation.
  • Typography tokens use standard Material typography scale; custom font families can override Roboto.
  • Motion spring parameters (damping 0.9, stiffness 1400) produce a physical, responsive feel appropriate for interactive components.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 dialogs expose two active token sets in the live token viewer: Dialog - Basic and Dialog - Full screen.
  • Basic dialogs use a 28dp extra-large container radius with level 3 elevation, while full-screen dialogs use a 0dp container radius and keep the main container at level 0.
  • Shared action affordances in both variants use label-large typography and primary-colored labels and state layers.
  • Basic dialog title text maps to headline-small and supporting text maps to body-medium; full-screen dialog headlines map to title-large.
  • Hover, focus, and pressed state-layer opacity tokens are surfaced through md.sys.state.*.state-layer-opacity system tokens.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat basic dialogs as surfaced cards with a surface-container-high fill, 28dp corners, 24dp outer padding, and min/max width constraints of 280dp to 560dp.
  • Reuse label-large typography for dialog actions in both variants, and map hover, focus, and pressed state opacities to the surfaced md.sys.state.*.state-layer-opacity tokens.
  • Full-screen dialogs keep the container, header, and action bar flat at rest, then elevate the header and action bar to level 2 while scrolling.
  • Basic dialog titles and subheads align to headline-small; full-screen headers align to title-large; supporting text aligns to body-medium.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 FAB specifications covering three current tonal color variants and three current size variants (baseline 56 dp, medium 80 dp, large 96 dp).
  • Four interactive states documented for color variants: Enabled, Hovered, Focused, and Pressed.
  • Color values were scraped from the live FAB token viewer resources for the Default / Light expressive context.
  • Baseline (default) size measurements come from the Specs page Measurements section; live token viewer omits a dedicated FAB - Size - Default table, so values are sourced from the FAB measurements diagram.
  • Deprecated baseline token sets, including Small FAB and legacy surface variants, are excluded from this document.

docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/icon-buttons/specs Collected: 2026-04-25

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 icon button specifications covering four color variants (Filled, Tonal, Outlined, Standard) and five size variants (Xsmall, Small, Medium, Large, Xlarge).
  • Five interactive states documented for color variants: Enabled, Disabled, Hovered, Focused, and Pressed.
  • Toggle icon button selected and unselected states are included where present in the MD3 token set.
  • Values and source tokens were scraped from the live token viewer payload for the Default / Light context.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Four token sets are exposed in the primary token viewer: baseline, common, vibrant, and standard.
  • Expressive menus use two color mappings: standard is surface-based and vibrant is tertiary-based.
  • The main page exposes baseline measurements as text, but the expressive vertical-menu measurements are image-only in the rendered page.
  • Baseline rows inside the shared token viewer include many entries marked as deprecated.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Prefer the expressive vertical-menu token sets for new work and keep the baseline set only for compatibility paths.
  • Treat standard and vibrant mappings as separate style families; their token namespaces and color roles differ materially.
  • Preserve support for hover, focus, pressed, disabled, and focus-indicator states because each token set exposes state-specific overrides.
  • Where the token viewer exposes shape or elevation only as previews, keep those values marked visual-only unless another MD3 source provides concrete numeric values.

docs.title: Progress Indicators MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/progress-indicators/specs Collected: 2026-03-12

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The primary token viewer exposes three non-deprecated token sets: shared common tokens plus linear and circular variant-specific baseline tokens.
  • Shared common tokens provide current color values and shape previews; the shape rows render as circular previews but do not expose textual numeric values.
  • Linear baseline geometry centers on a 4dp track, 10dp wavy height, 3dp wave amplitude, and 40dp wave wavelength, with a 20dp wavelength for indeterminate waves.
  • Circular baseline geometry centers on a 40dp size, 48dp wavy size, 4dp track thickness, 1.6dp wave amplitude, and 15dp wave wavelength.
  • The Measurements section explicitly states a 4dp screen-edge inset for linear indicators and defines amplitude and wavelength, but its remaining figure callouts are image-only in accessible text.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Model shared colors separately from variant-specific geometry. Linear and circular sizing is not encoded in the common token set.
  • Treat the shared shape tokens as fully rounded/circular until another source exposes a resolved radius token; the rendered token previews use a circular-shape class and no numeric text.
  • Support both flat and wavy linear indicators; expressive linear geometry depends on wave height, amplitude, and wavelength tokens rather than only track thickness.
  • Keep deprecated thick token groups out of default implementation paths unless you intentionally need archived compatibility behavior.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 text field specifications covering filled and outlined fields plus current select and autocomplete variants exposed in the live token viewer.
  • Five interactive states are represented across the current token sets: Enabled, Disabled, Hovered, Focused, and Error.
  • Values were resolved from the Material token table using the Light + Default + Expressive context when available, with Light + Default as fallback.
